messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: svc-scheduler error-rate (5xx/timeouts) crossed threshold (4.8%) in prod-eu for 5m. AlertID: ALRT-186543. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/scheduler/svc-scheduler

ria-oncall: I'm paged, looking. gateway 502/504 spikes, tracer shows requests stuck in batcher queue for >1.5s.

simon-eng: grabbing logs now — seeing repeated:
```
2026-06-02T10:01:12Z batcher: enqueue request id=abc123 size=20480 tokens wait_ms=1683
2026-06-02T10:01:13Z batcher: dequeue batch id=b-9c7 error=timeout downstream=runtime gateway=504
```

maya-sre: checking infra metrics — GPU util around 96% on batch pool nodes, CPU fine. batch_queue_length=12,400, avg_wait_ms=1720, 5xx_rate=5.6% (eu-west-1). Looks like headlock: a few large long-context requests are preventing smaller fast requests from going through.

devon-ml: FYI I rolled a batching heuristic tweak ~12m ago to prefer larger batches for throughput (flag: aggressive-batching=true). That could amplify HOL for short tails.

ria-oncall: OK probable cause = head-of-line blocking due to aggressive batching + long requests. Mitigations (immediate):
  1) reduce max batch token cap to favor smaller batches
  2) enable preemptive eviction of long-waiting requests
  3) route sub-200-token requests to low-latency pool
  4) add burst GPU capacity to dedicated pool (if needed)

Applying changes now. Commands:
```bash
redwoodctl config set svc-scheduler batching.max_batch_tokens=4096 --env=prod
redwoodctl feature toggle aggressive-batching --off --env=prod
redwoodctl feature toggle preemptive-eviction --on --env=prod
redwoodctl runtime scale pool-lowlatency --replicas 4 --env=prod
kubectl rollout restart deployment/svc-scheduler -n prod-batcher
```

simon-eng: executed the config change and triggered a rolling restart. deploy-bot: started rolling restart of 24 pods (batcher). version: svc-scheduler@2026.6.2. Awaiting pod readiness.

kai-support: customer impact — Zendesk spike: ~23 customers reporting elevated latencies and some 502s in last 10m. Top affected customers: aeroai, docscribe, quickforms (APAC & EU). Not full outage but degraded UX.

maya-sre: initial effects: after toggle off/aggressive-batching and restart, queue length dropped from 12.4k -> 4.2k in 3m. avg_wait_ms -> 420ms. 5xx_rate down from 5.6% -> 1.3% in eu-west-1. Still seeing tail in a subset of nodes (node-pool-b-7).

devon-ml: digging deeper — found long-context session (id=session-7f2) that produced continuous token generation for ~90s and held KV cache and batch slot. I'll kill orphaned session and add eviction. Command:
```bash
redwoodctl sessions evict --session=session-7f2 --env=prod --reason="long-context runaway"
```

simon-eng: evicted session, also pushed a quick guard: max_session_tokens=65536 -> 32768 to prevent single req hogging.

maya-sre: routing tweak: set routing policy to route small requests (<200 tokens) to pool-lowlatency for next 30m.

ria-oncall: Requesting burst capacity — @lee-engineering-manager can we approve temporary GPU burst (+8 vGPUs) to dedicated batch pool? ETA ~8m on infra side if approved. :point_up:

lee-engineering-manager: Approved. Infra to add 8 vGPUs to prod-dedicated-pool now. ETA 7-10m. I'll follow up on slack infra channel.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollout complete. 24/24 pods ready.

maya-sre: metrics update 6m after mitigations: batch_queue_length=1.1k, avg_wait_ms=160ms, 5xx_rate=0.6% global. EU hotspot improved but keep monitoring. Logging shows reduced dequeue timeouts.

ria-oncall: Good progress. Current status: partial mitigation successful, customer impact-contained (degraded for ~18m). Actions remaining: monitor for 30m, keep burst capacity until baseline stable, follow-up postmortem to rollback heuristic tweak or find better gating.

devon-ml: I'll add a canary + regression test for batching heuristic that simulates mixed short/long requests to prevent this regress in the future.

kai-support: continuing to triage customer tickets; sending an incident update to impacted customers with ETA for resolution and mitigation notes.

ria-oncall: handing off monitoring to maya-sre for the next 45m — I'm stepping out for a scheduled meeting. If error rate climbs above 2% re-paging oncall.

maya-sre: acknowledged, taking over monitoring. I'll post a short note in #incidents-summary when we hit 30m stable.

ria-oncall: quick post-incident checklist (to-do):
  - devon: add regression test + revert/soften heuristic (due EOD)
  - eng: add alert on batch_queue_longtail (per-node) to catch headlock earlier
  - infra: document burst capacity runbook and threshold for auto-burst
  - support: send follow-up to affected customers summarizing impact and remediation

lee-engineering-manager: leave a calendar entry for postmortem sync tomorrow 09:30. cc: eng, ml, infra, support.

incident-bot: NOTE: Incident ALRT-186543 is now in "mitigated" state. Monitoring active.

maya-sre: 30m stable check-in: 5xx_rate sustained <0.8%, avg latency back to baseline. Marking thread for postmortem and closing pager. :thumbsup:

ria-oncall: thanks all — great quick coordination. I'll add RFC for batching policy changes.

simon-eng: saving logs and timeline to /incidents/1865432100/ for postmortem writeup.

maya-sre: handing off final watch to next oncall. Closing this thread.
